issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases

  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
The aurora integration is not being loaded. I keep getting the error below.


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.15 
- Integration causing this issue: `aurora`
- Link to integration documentation on our website: [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/aurora/](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/aurora/)

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
binary_sensor:
  - platform: aurora
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.binary_sensor
Source: components/aurora/binary_sensor.py:114
Integration: Binary sensor (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 10:06:37 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 10:06:37 PM

Error while setting up aurora platform for binary_sensor
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 197, in _async_setup_platform
    await asyncio.shield(task)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 57, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/aurora/binary_sensor.py", line 49, in setup_platform
    aurora_data.update()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/util/__init__.py", line 239, in wrapper
    result = method(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/aurora/binary_sensor.py", line 114, in update
    if int(self.visibility_level) > self.threshold:
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'Found</title>'
```

## Additional information
comments: It looks like `http://services.swpc.noaa.gov/text/aurora-nowcast-map.txt` is no longer available. After a little digging around I found `https://services.swpc.noaa.gov/json/ovation_aurora_latest.json` which might be potential replacement.

review_comments: We don't need to add the domain to the unique id. The config entries handler is aware of the flow domain already.

If this is a service we should return that as entry type here.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/device_registry_index#device-properties
This is already done by the parent class.

The aurora library is using aiohttp. `ConnectionError` is not an aiohttp exception. We should probably either catch an aiohttp error or a library specific error here.

https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_reference.html#client-exceptions
We need to set up the integration, ie set up the config entry, before starting the options flow to make sure the config flow module is loaded. Set up the entry with `hass.config_entries.async_setup`.
The block till done should be moved to within the patch context manager.

Fixed this comment and the bottom one here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/43128
You're now fetching the data twice. Would you be able to use `coordinator.last_update_success` to check if something didn't go right?
Oh, you already do that. Why do you also do the check above? That seems double, you should drop that one.

Sorry - reviewed a couple other integrations and I see what you're calling out. I have removed the initial connectivity check since there is no need to validate anything but connectivity which happens in the coordinator anyway.
